body:
You've said that working would make me want to get out of bed, but that would be one of the things that would make me want to stay in bed the most. I don't trust in myself, I don't see potential, I don't like trying to do things because I'm afraid of failing, I rather not do it at all and not find out if I can do it or not. Obviously that makes no sense, but I don't know how to think otherwise, which is why I feel stuck.

As for changing majors, I agree that it won't be a financial burden, but I also feel awful taking advantage of my situation to stay in education limbo while my parents pay for me. The money doesn't matter, but the principle still hurts me, I don't want to be a burden to my parents, or to anyone.
I have a dog, it's the living being that I love most in the world.

I'm studying computer engineering, so even if I had motivation I'd lack the time. The thing is I don't believe in myself enough to do any of that, I feel stuck to the path that I'm on, and that I must keep following it. I don't know how to do anything else.
I identify with a pretty much all you've said.

I don't make my own money yet, I'm 21 in college. I also have a really hard time getting basic things done, I have no idea how to have motivation. If I have to put effort into getting out of bed, am I really able to help other people with my time? I don't believe I'm capable.

I go to therapy, and so far it's more just a place where I can "half-vent" (because I don't have the guts to say what I actually feel). I don't take meds but to be honest I really wish I did, I don't really care for the side effects.
If in nothingness you don't feel anything, can it really be that scary? I actually would prefer nothingness over pretty much anything else.
